notes: Roster follows the 26 rows of Table A1 (I:p7-b0; caption T:p7-b0), described as the 26 HVSs studied in this work (T:p6-b50). The paper defines an HVS as a star that will escape the Milky Way (T:p1-b9) and calls the sample previously known/confirmed hypervelocity stars (T:p1-b6, T:p1-b10), so all entries are follow_up. HVS2 is grouped with US708 (T:p2-b10) and HVS3 with HE 0437-5439 (T:p1-b9); HVS3's LMC-origin conclusion does not remove its prior Galactic unbound-candidate status. The range 'HVS4 through HVS24 excluding HVS11' (T:p1-b9) would mention HVS14 and HVS23, but neither appears as a separate tabulated row; the only tabulated named stars without HVS numbers are HD271791 and HIP60350, and the paper states no explicit HVS14/HVS23 correspondence, so I do not merge them speculatively. HVS11 is expressly excluded.

HVS1: HVS1 is listed in Table A1 (T:p7-b0) with right ascension and declination in sexagesimal notation; RA uses units of hours (hourangle), Dec degrees. The v_hel column is taken as the heliocentric radial velocity. No parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability is reported specifically for HVS1 in the supplied material.

HVS2: Target is HVS2 (US708). Table A1 lists R.A. in sexagesimal form and Dec. in sexagesimal form; values are recorded as printed. The distance and radial velocity in Table A1 (8.5 ± 1 kpc, 917 ± 7 km/s) match the values quoted in the Introduction (8.5 ± 1.0 kpc, 917 ± 7 km/s, Geier et al. 2015). No parallax, galactocentric radius, rest-frame velocity, or bound probabilities specific to HVS2 are reported.

HVS3: The reported ejection/relative velocities with respect to the LMC (e.g. 870^{+69}_{-66} km/s) are not heliocentric radial velocities or Galactic-rest-frame speeds and are therefore not recorded in those quantity fields. The 40^{+11}_{-10} kpc value in T:p2-b14 is the distance of the past closest approach to the Milky Way, not the present-day galactocentric radius. No parallax, Galactic-rest-frame total speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS3 is reported.

HVS4: Table A1 (T:p7-b0) reports only the listed position, proper motion, heliocentric radial velocity, and heliocentric distance for HVS4. No individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS4 is reported in the supplied material.

HVS5: HVS5 is listed in Table A1. The table does not report a parallax, current Galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS5, so those quantities are not extracted. Right ascension is retained in sexagesimal hourangle notation and declination in sexagesimal degrees without conversion. The table caption states that almost all proper motions are from Gaia DR2 except for HVS1, HVS4, HVS13, and HIP60350; HVS5 is not among those exceptions.

HVS7: Table A1 (T:p7-b0) lists the adopted present-day HVS7 data. The table's RA proper-motion column is μ_α cos δ. No individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS7.
HVS8: HVS8 is listed only in Table A1 (T:p7-b0; I:p7-b0). The paper does not report a parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS8.

HVS9: The HVS9 row of Table A1 (T:p7-b0, I:p7-b0) reports position, proper motion, heliocentric radial velocity, and heliocentric distance. The tabulated proper-motion RA component is μ_α cos δ. No HVS9-specific parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is numerically reported. HVS9 appears graphically in Figure 1's origin-probability panel (I:p3-b1), but no exact values for HVS9 are stated.
HVS10: Table A1 (T:p7-b0) is the only HVS10-specific numerical entry; no HVS10 parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported.

HVS12: HVS12 values are from Table A1 (T:p7-b0). The tabulated proper-motion RA component is μ_α cos δ. The paper does not report an individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS12.

HVS13: HVS13's Table A1 row reports no parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability, so those quantities are omitted. The Table A1 caption (T:p7-b0) states that HVS13 is one of the stars for which the proper motion is not from Gaia DR2; its listed reference is Ref. 1 (Brown et al. 2015).

HVS16: Table A1 (LOCATION T:p7-b0; also image LOCATION I:p7-b0) reports HVS16's equatorial coordinates, proper motions, heliocentric radial velocity, and heliocentric distance. The table lists HVS16 proper motions with refs. 2,4; the caption states almost all proper motions are from Gaia DR2 except HVS1, HVS4, HVS13, and HIP60350, so HVS16's proper motions are adopted as Gaia DR2. The paper does not report an individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS16.

HVS17: HVS17 values are taken from Table A1. Right ascension is sexagesimal hours:minutes:seconds, and declination is sexagesimal degrees:arcminutes:arcseconds. The paper does not report HVS17-specific parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability; these were not inferred.

HVS18: HVS18 is identified in Table A1. The paper reports no individual bound/unbound probability, Galactocentric radius, or Galactic rest-frame velocity for HVS18. The table's proper-motion correlation for HVS18 is 0.213.

HVS19: Values for HVS19 are taken from Table A1 (also shown in the table image at I:p7-b0). The paper does not report HVS19's parallax, current galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability; the probabilities in Figure 1 concern passing within 5 kpc of the MW or LMC, not bound probability.

HVS21: HVS21 is listed in Table A1 at T:p7-b0 (and shown in the table image I:p7-b0). The right ascension is sexagesimal hours and the declination sexagesimal degrees. No individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HVS21.

HVS22: All HVS22 values come from its row in Table A1 (T:p7-b0). The table caption states that proper motions are from Gaia DR2 except for HVS1, HVS4, HVS13, and HIP60350; HVS22 is therefore a Gaia DR2 proper-motion row. No individual parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HVS22 is reported.

HVS24: The right ascension is reported as sexagesimal hours:minutes:seconds (unit hourangle). The paper does not report a parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for HVS24. No HVS24-specific orbital results are given in the text; Figure 4 concerns a mock sample rather than HVS24 itself.

LAMOST-HVS1: Table A1 (T:p7-b0; I:p7-b0) provides the present-day equatorial coordinates, proper motions, heliocentric radial velocity, and heliocentric distance for LAMOST-HVS1. No parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported specifically for this star. The probabilities in Figure 1 (T:p3-b1; I:p3-b1) are probabilities of passing within 5 kpc of the Milky Way/LMC, not bound/unbound probabilities.

LAMOST-HVS2: Table A1 (T:p7-b0) reports only the listed astrometry, heliocentric radial velocity, and heliocentric distance for LAMOST-HVS2; no parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

LAMOST-HVS3: The paper's detailed HVS3 results (including the 870 km/s ejection velocity, LMC-origin probabilities, and black-hole constraints) refer to HVS3/HE 0437-5439, which is distinct from the target LAMOST-HVS3. No values of parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability are reported specifically for LAMOST-HVS3.

HD271791: The target is listed as HD271791 in Table A1. Its position, proper motions, heliocentric radial velocity, and heliocentric distance are reported there; no parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic-rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for this star.

HIP60350: The paper reports no parallax, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for HIP60350. The table caption states that HIP60350 is one of the stars whose proper-motion measurements are not from Gaia DR2; its row lists reference 8 (Irrgang et al. 2010).
